newsitem.title: SHARJAH: CRICKET-PAKISTAN OVERWHELM SRI LANKA TO CLAIM FINAL SPOT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN OVERWHELM SRI LANKA TO CLAIM FINAL SPOT.

text.p: A supremely confident Pakistan virtually toyed with world champions Sri Lanka, chalking up a convincing eight-wicket victory to become the first team to enter the final of the Singer Champions Trophy cricket tournament on Tuesday.

Chasing a modest 190 for victory, Pakistan were off to a brilliant start with their elegant openers -- Saeed Anwar and Aamir Sohail -- scoring runs almost at will against a surprisingly subdued Sri Lanka side.
Anwar, the most aggressive of the two, slammed a chanceless 112, his second century in the tournament and 11th of his career, spanning 112 matches while Sohail cracked a solid 65 off 126 balls.
The two were involved in a match-winning stand of 173 runs in 39.1 overs before Sohail's uppish drive landed in the safe hands of Sajeeva de Silva in the deep.
The match was reduced to a formality which Pakistan completed without any fuss, though they did lose Hasan Raza, the young test star, cheaply.

Sri Lanka, with three points in four matches, must now await the outcome of Wednesday's match between New Zealand and Pakistan. If New Zealand win they go to the final. If they lose, run-rate will decide.
Earlier, Marvan Atapattu led a Sri Lankan recovery with a sensible 58 after the feared Pakistan pace attack reduced them to 31-3 in 6.5 overs.

Atapattu, playing each delivery on merit, led the revival in the company of a dour Hashan Tillakeratne, and the two put on 75 runs for the fourth wicket. Tillakeratne, who edged a Mushtaq Ahmed delivery to wicketkeeper Moin Jhan, scored 34.
Just when Atapattu began to open up he ran himself out, failing to beat a Waqar Younis throw from deep.
Waqar had a great day in the field, taking three for 28 and securing an earlier run-out.
